note: A product is a MIX of profiles, never one label. Weights are evidence-derived from the brief and the repository, and low confidence must weaken every downstream decision instead of being rounded up to a guess. See README.md. detectionKeywords let the compliance gate tell WHICH kind of product a plan describes from the plan's own words, so that a duty scoped to one profile is not reported against every other one.
schemaChange: v2 replaces the single valuePath with valuePaths, a list. A product can carry several value chains that break INDEPENDENTLY - a marketplace with a flawless buyer journey and no way to list an item is dead, and an ERP whose money ledger is perfect while its stock figures lie stops production. Since value multiplies along a chain, multiple chains multiply with each other too: one intact chain does not rescue a product whose second chain is broken. A single-path schema could not express that, so the completeness check could not look for it. v3 adds acceptanceRule, one rule rather than a chain per profile, because acceptance is not a new journey but the existing ones under a change of quantifier.

acceptanceRule.appliesTo: every profile, instantiated against whatever valuePaths it declares
requires: the deployed instance is reachable by the client from outside the factory
it holds content sufficient to exercise every link of every declared path
one complete traversal of each path has been performed on that instance
the instance is recognisably the client's own - their data, their language
acceptanceRule.quantifier: Not a seventeenth chain. Every valuePath already states what must be POSSIBLE; the acceptance rule states that at least one complete traversal of it has ACTUALLY been performed, by the client, on the deployed instance, against real content. Same chain, existential instead of universal, and a possibility claim is not witnessed by another possibility claim.
acceptanceRule.witness: witnessed(P) = the product over every declared path of the fraction of its links actually traversed. No threshold: value multiplies along a chain, so one unwalked link makes the product zero and a partial traversal witnesses nothing. This is the same multiplicativity that governs construction, applied to demonstration.
acceptanceRule.reasoning: Every valuePath traces the END USER's journey. None traces the buyer's: how does the client see that what they paid for exists and runs? The factory reaches DELIVERED on merge counts, which is a claim about what was built and not about what was shown. A product can be perfect for its users and undemonstrable to its buyer, so this fails independently of every other chain and must be judged separately. Carries no measured number, per the 'derived' rule - refutable by argument.
acceptanceRule.source: Derived from domain reasoning, stated 2026-08-16 (closes F30 and F21). Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status.

profiles.source: Derived from domain reasoning about what this class of product must contain to deliver its value, stated 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
profiles.reasoning: An order is an object with states: it must be findable, priced, paid for, confirmed, delivered, and - because consumers change their minds and the law lets them - returnable. Each state is a place the object can get stuck; a chain missing one of them describes a shop that cannot complete the transaction it exists for.

profiles.title: Appointment or resource booking

valuePaths.evidence: observed 2026-08-15: 'get a reminder' claimed by 4/4 surveyed products; 'reschedule or cancel' claimed by only 1/4 - the weakest-advertised link in the chain

valuePaths.note: Breaks independently of the customer chain: a booking product nobody on staff can actually run gets abandoned even when customers can book perfectly.

profiles.source: Derived from domain reasoning about what this class of product must contain to deliver its value, stated 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
profiles.note: Surveyed 2026-08-15 across 4 real German booking products. Reminders (4/4) and no-show or waiting-list handling (4/4) are universally advertised - the market treats them as table stakes, and a client brief almost never asks for either. Self-service cancellation by the customer is advertised by only 1 of 4, which is the asymmetry worth acting on: every vendor sells reminders as the cure for no-shows, yet a reminder only tells you someone is coming, while a self-cancellation gives the hour back and lets it be rebooked. The survey measures what vendors ADVERTISE, not what products contain, so it is evidence about market expectation, not about implementations.
profiles.reasoning: A booking commits a scarce resource - an hour of someone's time - which is why the chain has two ends. The customer's end fails by not turning up; the staff's end fails by nobody being able to run the day. Both destroy the same slot.

profiles.title: Customer relationship management

valuePaths.note: The object here is a RELATIONSHIP over time, not a task - which is why this is not the same profile as an internal operations tool. A lead lost between stages is money lost invisibly: nobody can see what did not happen.

profiles.source: Derived from domain reasoning about what this class of product must contain to deliver its value, stated 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
profiles.note: Rarely commissioned whole on these markets - mature packaged CRMs exist and clients buy them. Real requests concentrate on integration with an ERP or accounting system, data migration off a legacy tool, and a pipeline shaped to a non-standard sales process. The full chain is recorded anyway, because a request for one fragment still has to fit the whole.
profiles.reasoning: The object is a relationship persisting across contacts, not a task. Every stage boundary is a place a lead is dropped, and the loss is invisible because nobody can see the deal that did not happen.

profiles.title: Stock, purchasing and order handling (Warenwirtschaft)

valuePaths.note: The material chain. When stock figures lie, work stops regardless of how correct the money is.
The money chain runs in parallel and breaks independently. Both must hold: they are multiplied, not averaged.

profiles.source: Derived from domain reasoning about what this class of product must contain to deliver its value, stated 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
profiles.note: In Germany this is the most established packaged-software category for mid-sized business, so a full custom build is unusual. Requests arrive as fragments: bills of materials and production steps for a small manufacturer, or a bridge between a shop and an existing Warenwirtschaft system.
profiles.reasoning: Goods and money move through the business in parallel and are reconciled against each other. The two chains are separate because they fail separately: wrong stock stops production while the ledger stays perfect, and vice versa.

profiles.title: Content management and publishing

valuePaths.note: Reversibility is the defining property, not publishing: the cost of a mistake in public text is asymmetric, so unpublishing and rolling back matter more than the act of putting something live. 'Learn it has gone stale' was missing until 2026-08-16 and is the link that makes reversibility reachable: 'update or unpublish' is an action nobody performs until something tells them the text no longer holds. Without it the chain silently assumes the editor already knows, which is true only on the day they published it.

A separate path, not a step in the editor's, because it breaks independently and serves a different person: an editorial workflow can be perfect while nobody can answer what exists. GQM telemetry does not substitute - telemetry measures whether the SYSTEM works, this answers what the COLLECTION holds, and the two are different questions with different readers.

profiles.source: Derived from domain reasoning about what this class of product must contain to deliver its value, stated 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
profiles.note: Rarely built from scratch - WordPress and similar dominate. Real requests are usually integration with an inventory or CRM system, or a workflow that packaged tools cannot express.
profiles.reasoning: Content is published to an audience, which makes the cost of a mistake asymmetric and public. Reversibility - unpublishing, rolling back - is therefore a stronger requirement than publishing itself. Published content also DECAYS while nothing happens to it, which is the one failure mode no action in the workflow produces: the chain up to 'publish' describes work someone is doing, and staleness is the state a document reaches by nobody doing anything. A chain built only from actions cannot represent it, which is why it was missing.

profiles.title: Document approval and signing

valuePaths.note: Retrieval is the link that decides whether the product was worth building, and it is the one nobody demonstrates at handover. Retrieval alone is not enough, though, and this is worse here than in a CMS: finding a superseded contract or an obsolete regulation and believing it current is more damaging than finding nothing at all, because the user acts on it. Added 2026-08-16.

path: see what has expired or been superseded
valuePaths.note: Breaks independently of the originator's path and answers a different person's question. For a body of normative documents this is the governing need, not a report bolted on: the collection's own state IS the product.

profiles.source: Derived from domain reasoning about what this class of product must contain to deliver its value, stated 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
profiles.reasoning: A document is created to be relied upon later. Approval and signature establish that reliance; retrieval years afterwards is what the whole exercise was for, and it is the step nobody demonstrates at handover. Reliance is also what makes staleness dangerous rather than untidy here: a retrieved document that is silently out of date is acted upon, so 'found' and 'still true' must be different states the product can tell apart.

profiles.title: Computer or mobile game

path: understand what to do within minutes
be given a reason to return
valuePaths.note: Nothing downstream exists if this chain breaks, and it breaks silently.
The one chain that cannot be compensated for. A game with excellent art, story, economy and infrastructure but a dull core loop is worth nothing, and every other chain multiplies against this one.

valuePaths.appliesWhen: the game sells anything inside itself
valuePaths.note: The 'not regret it' link is where the enforcement actions land, and it is the link no brief ever asks for. See the purchase-transparency capability: both FTC cases turned on exactly this step.

valuePaths.appliesWhen: the game has chat, multiplayer or player-created content
valuePaths.note: Adding this chain has a legal price, not only an engineering one - under §24a JuSchG chat functions are a rating factor that can raise the game's age label and so shrink its lawful audience. It also brings platform duties around user content that need checking case by case; the corpus does not yet hold a verified citation for those, so they must be raised as an open question rather than assumed.

profiles.source: Derived from domain reasoning about what this class of product must contain to deliver its value, stated 2026-08-15. Carries no measured share by rule - see README.md on the 'derived' status. Refutable by argument.
profiles.note: TWO WAYS THIS PROFILE DIFFERS FROM EVERY OTHER ONE IN THIS FILE, both of which change how it must be decomposed. FIRST: there is no external need pushing the user forward. A buyer in a shop already wants the goods and will complain when a step is broken; a player owes the game nothing, so a broken link produces silent abandonment and no report. Outcome measurement is therefore not a nice-to-have epic here - it is the ONLY channel through which failure is observable at all. SECOND: capability completeness does not imply value. For a transactional product, a complete and working chain is most of the job. For a game it is a floor and nothing more - fun does not decompose into features, and a game can satisfy every requirement in this corpus and still be worthless. So the floors in the compiler prompt must be treated here as a minimum that says nothing about whether the product is good, and no completeness check may be read as evidence that it is. THE LEGAL WEIGHT IS CONDITIONAL, NOT INHERENT. Every statutory entry attached to this profile now carries appliesWhenKeywords and fires only when the plan shows the condition actually holds: age labelling when the game is published or distributed, structural precautions when it has chat, multiplayer or purchases, parental consent when it collects personal data. A game that sells nothing, collects nothing and is not distributed - a classroom or jam project - therefore inherits none of them, and must not be told to disclose loot-box odds it does not have. What remains for such a game is the part that decides whether it is any good: the first session and the core loop, neither of which any law has an opinion about.
profiles.reasoning: A player owes the product nothing, so the chain must manufacture the desire it then satisfies. The first session establishes whether there is a second; the core loop is what the rest multiplies against.
